title: Using default_factory=list for multi-valued parameter in Query model leads to memory leak
body:
### First Check

- [X] I added a very descriptive title here.
- [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search.
- [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information.
- [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer.
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import FastAPI, Query
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

app = FastAPI()


class QueryParams(BaseModel):
    category: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)


@app.get("/items")
def read_items(params: Annotated[QueryParams, Query()]) -> list[str]:
    return []
```


### Description

- Start the app using `fastapi run` and observe initial memory usage
- Hit `http://localhost:8000/items` multiple times
- See the memory usage now, it may have increased

Or execute this

```py
import time
from httpx import Client


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for i in range(5):  # 5 rounds
        if i > 0:
            time.sleep(3)  # give some time between rounds
        for j in range(100):  # 100 requests per round
            with Client(base_url="http://localhost:8000") as client:
                client.get("/items")
```

```bash
(fastapi-query) anilk@Anils-MacBook-Pro fastapi-query % ps -o rss -p 21243 # Grab the PID
   RSS
 75072 # initial at startup

(fastapi-query) anilk@Anils-MacBook-Pro fastapi-query % python3 test_api.py
(fastapi-query) anilk@Anils-MacBook-Pro fastapi-query % ps -o rss -p 21243 
   RSS
 92592 # +17MB

(fastapi-query) anilk@Anils-MacBook-Pro fastapi-query % python3 test_api.py
(fastapi-query) anilk@Anils-MacBook-Pro fastapi-query % ps -o rss -p 21243 
   RSS
109296 # +16MB

(fastapi-query) anilk@Anils-MacBook-Pro fastapi-query % python3 test_api.py
(fastapi-query) anilk@Anils-MacBook-Pro fastapi-query % ps -o rss -p 21243 
   RSS
125824 # +16MB
```


### Operating System

macOS

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.135.1

### Pydantic Version

2.12.5

### Python Version

Python 3.14.2

### Additional Context

Changing to below fixes the leak

```py
class QueryParams(BaseModel):
    category: list[str] | None = Field(default=None)
```

```bash
(fastapi-query) anilk@Anils-MacBook-Pro fastapi-query % ps -o rss -p 29649
   RSS
 75184
(fastapi-query) anilk@Anils-MacBook-Pro fastapi-query % python3 test_api.py
(fastapi-query) anilk@Anils-MacBook-Pro fastapi-query % ps -o rss -p 29649 
   RSS
 76352
(fastapi-query) anilk@Anils-MacBook-Pro fastapi-query % python3 test_api.py
(fastapi-query) anilk@Anils-MacBook-Pro fastapi-query % ps -o rss -p 29649 
   RSS
 76688
(fastapi-query) anilk@Anils-MacBook-Pro fastapi-query % python3 test_api.py
(fastapi-query) anilk@Anils-MacBook-Pro fastapi-query % ps -o rss -p 29649 
   RSS
 76880
```

Try watching longer and you will likely notice that it reduces (I checked and it worked for me on Ubuntu).

Garbage collector doesn't free the memory immediately. I think this is the reason
